rfm_tuples.R: 'As of December 31, 2023, the Company was in compliance with the financial covenants in our Credit Agreement.' (MD&A, Liquidity) + 'The Credit Agreement includes various covenants, including total net leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio financial covenants.' (Note 9 Debt)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify covenant-compliance language continuity across 10-Q Q1'24 (filed 2024-05-03). Mode B — derive: if compliance is genuinely uncontested, no covenant relief amendment should be needed AND insiders should not be heavily diluted; check Amendment cadence and Amendment No. 3 size relative to the existing $300M facility.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1'24 10-Q REPEATS verbatim 'in compliance with the financial covenants' (line 3148). However, AMENDMENT CADENCE is high: Amendment No. 1 (May 17, 2023 — extended term-loan draw window and repayment start), Amendment No. 2 (October 24, 2023 — consent for Horizon Transaction, filed contemporaneously with deal announcement), Amendment No. 3 (April 1, 2024 — $225M incremental delayed-draw term-loan + $50M revolver upsize, closed on the same day as the Horizon acquisition). Three amendments in 11 months on a 3-year-old facility. Cash and cash equivalents reported as $390M at 3/31/24 (up from $139M at YE23) — driven by $305.8M tower sale proceeds (Mar 29, 2024) and timing of pre-closing of Horizon funding.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The compliance claim is literally true (and structurally so, since the heaviest debt has not yet drawn — $300M term loans only carry a 4.0x leverage covenant trigger for unlimited dividends, with stepped restrictions above 4.0x). Amendment cadence is high but ALL three amendments are growth-related (draw-period extensions, Horizon consent, upsizing) rather than covenant-relief waivers. No language suggests a near-miss or going-concern doubt. Genuinely benign on this axis.

rfm_tuples.R: Auditor language: '/s/ RSM US LLP ... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2022.' AND '/s/ KPMG LLP ... We served as the Company's auditor from 2001 to 2022.' (10-K F-3 / F-5)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify auditor identity and tenure. Mode B — derive: a 22-year KPMG (Big 4) relationship ending in 2022 in favor of RSM US LLP (mid-tier) coincident with the company's transition to high-capex FTTH overbuild model and the discontinued-Wireless sale ($1.945B from T-Mobile in 2021) requires examination of WHY KPMG was replaced; check 8-K Item 4.01 for the reason and any Item 304 disagreements.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar.list_filings(0000354963) for 8-K Item 4.01 in 2022 + 10-K Item 9 / Note disclosure in 2022 10-K (referenced here)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Item 9 of this 10-K states 'CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE' and contains NO disclosed disagreements (lines 2656-2660). Auditor downgrade is from BIG 4 (KPMG) to TIER 2 (RSM US LLP) after a 21-year continuous engagement — uncommon for a company of SHEN's size (~$0.7B market cap pre-cutoff) unless audit-fee pressure or a dispute drove the change. However, the 2022 transition pre-dates the current 10-K and would have required an 8-K Item 4.01 with letter from former auditor at that time. The absence of an ongoing Item 304 disagreement in either the 2022 or 2023 10-K is materially exculpatory.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor downgrade from Big 4 to mid-tier is a yellow flag that the framework should flag at any distressed name, but in this case the change occurred ~18 months before the cutoff and no current-period disagreement is disclosed. RSM US LLP is a legitimate PCAOB-registered firm (#49) and the ICFR attestation is unqualified. The combination of 'continuing major audit' (RSM has now served two full years) + 'unqualified opinion' + 'effective ICFR' makes this a moderate (not severe) concern. Downgrade likely cost-driven post-Wireless divestiture, not quality-driven.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The Broadband segment served 235,298 Revenue Generating Units (RGUs) at December 31, 2023, representing an increase of 6.5%, from December 31, 2022.' (Item 1) + KPI table showing Broadband Data RGUs 151,389 (2023) vs 133,930 (2022) vs 117,722 (2021)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the headline 6.5% RGU growth claim. Mode B — DECOMPOSE: derive whether the growth is driven by (a) the legacy cable footprint (incumbent, mature) vs (b) the new Glo Fiber overbuild footprint, and whether incumbent cable is actually SHRINKING despite the aggregate growth.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Broadband KPI table (lines 2030-2155) + Q1'24 10-Q Broadband KPI table (lines 3029-3055)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K data: Broadband Data RGUs by market — Cable Markets 109,679 (2023) vs 109,644 (2022) vs 106,345 (2021): essentially FLAT in 2023 and only +3.1% in 2022. Glo Fiber Markets 41,710 (2023) vs 24,286 (2022) vs 11,377 (2021): +71.7% YoY in 2023. Q1'24 update: Cable Markets data RGUs 108,958 (3/31/24) vs 109,920 (3/31/23) — DOWN -0.9% YoY for the first time. Cable broadband-data penetration is dropping (50.3% → 51.8%), and total broadband-data penetration is dropping from 36.8% → 32.7% as Glo Fiber adds more passings faster than it adds subscribers. Video RGUs declined 15.1% YoY (cord-cutting). Voice RGUs are flattish.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The headline '6.5% RGU growth' is a true claim that obscures Mode-B reality: the incumbent (mature, profitable) Cable broadband-data subscriber base inflected to OUTRIGHT DECLINE in Q1'24, while growth is concentrated in Glo Fiber — a brand still in capital-build mode where unit economics depend on penetration ramps. Bear case: cable cash flow funds Glo Fiber capex; if cable cash flow rolls over too fast, the overbuild thesis breaks. Not a lie, but the segment composition is the real risk this 10-K underplays. Mode-B finding.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The discontinuation of the FCC's ACP may adversely impact our Broadband revenue ... ACP is expected to end in April 2024 unless Congress passes legislation to increase the funding to support this program.' (Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify whether SHEN quantifies ACP-exposed subscribers anywhere in the filings. Mode B — derive: if the risk is material, the disclosure should be specific (number of subscribers, % of broadband revenue); silence on quantification is itself a signal of either (a) immaterial exposure or (b) refusal to quantify.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Risk Factors (line 1695) + 10-K KPI tables + Q1'24 10-Q Risk Factors (line 3174)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K does NOT quantify ACP-exposed subscribers or revenue. Q1'24 10-Q states (line 3174): 'As of March 31, 2024, the Company has not identified any needed updates to the risk factors included in our most recent Form 10-K.' Given SHEN serves rural/exurban Virginia/WV/Maryland/PA/KY (where ACP penetration tends to be higher than urban average), the absence of quantification while peers (e.g., Charter, Comcast) typically disclose ACP-subscriber counts is notable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Cannot confirm or deny materiality from local filings alone. The lack of quantification could reflect either immateriality (in which case the boilerplate Risk Factor is over-conservative) or selective disclosure. Neutral signal — Mode-B yellow flag rather than a deception finding.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We may incur more churn than estimated from our largest customer. Shentel estimates the remaining revenue churn from T-Mobile to be approximately $1 million for the Broadband segment and $2 million for the Tower segment.' (Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify Tower-segment T-Mobile churn estimate against the Q1'24 segment results and the Vertical Bridge tower-sale price ($309.9M, March 29, 2024). Mode B — derive: a tower-portfolio sale to Vertical Bridge for $309.9M (vs SHEN's market cap of ~$0.7B) is large enough that the sale itself answers the customer-concentration risk by transferring it to the buyer — what does that mean for residual SHEN concentration?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K line 1595 (T-Mobile churn estimate) + Q1'24 10-Q lines 2799-2810 (Tower Transaction) + Q1'24 segment data (Commercial Fiber revenue -19.8% YoY 'primarily driven by the expected decline in T-Mobile revenue from prior period backhaul circuit disconnects as part of the previously disclosed decommissioning of the former Sprint network')
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1'24 Commercial Fiber revenue declined 19.8% YoY (line 2995), with explicit attribution to T-Mobile/Sprint decommissioning — i.e., the disclosed $1M Broadband-segment T-Mobile churn was REAL and is now flowing through results. Tower segment SOLD entirely (initial 99.5% closed Mar 29, 2024; $309.9M total consideration, $305.8M net) — the customer-concentration risk in Tower was monetized rather than mitigated. Residual SHEN is now pure-play Broadband.

The Tower Transaction is a textbook example of management taking action on a disclosed risk — selling the concentrated asset at ~10-12x EBITDA (based on the disclosed tower segment metrics) when growth has plateaued and the customer is decommissioning. Clean execution, strong PASS on the disclosure-vs-action axis.

rfm_tuples.R: Implicit claim through dividend policy disclosure: 'Under the Company's credit agreement, the Company is restricted in its ability to pay dividends ... when the Company's Total Net Leverage Ratio ... is greater than 4.00:1.00 on a pro forma basis, an amount equal to the greater of 6.0% of the net cash proceeds from any public equity issuance ... or 4.0% of the estimated fair market value ... when the Company's Total Net Leverage ... is less than or equal to 4.00:1.00 on a pro forma basis, an unlimited amount.' (Dividend Policy) + dividend table
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify whether SHEN is currently paying dividends and whether the trajectory implies leverage above or below 4.0x. Mode B — derive: with $300M term debt at YE'23 against ~$60M-$80M EBITDA run-rate (back-of-envelope from $271M revenue and segment margins), pro-forma leverage post-Horizon-close is the key liquidity question.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Dividend Policy (lines 1866-1888) + 10-K Indebtedness (line 2607) + Q1'24 pro-forma debt-net-of-cash $190M (line 3129)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash dividends: $0.30/share in 2023 (Q1-Q4 quarterly), unchanged from 2022, plus a $18.75/share SPECIAL dividend in 2021 from the Wireless sale proceeds. SHEN has not cut the ordinary dividend, but the 2021 special dividend distributed most of the $1.945B T-Mobile proceeds back to shareholders rather than retaining for Glo Fiber capex — meaning the company chose external financing (Term Loans, ECP Preferred, tower sale) over retained cash. Q1'24 reports pro-forma debt-net-of-cash of $190M after Horizon close + ECP + tower sale. Pre-Horizon EBITDA was modest (operating loss $7.96M FY23 from continuing ops; need to add D&A ~$72M+ for EBITDA proxy ~$64M) — pro-forma EBITDA must include Horizon contribution to keep leverage below 4.0x.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 4.0x leverage covenant is a soft cap on growth strategy more than a near-term covenant risk. The 2021 special dividend in retrospect looks like a strategic choice that prioritized shareholder return over self-funded growth — leaving SHEN structurally reliant on capital markets to fund the Glo Fiber buildout and the Horizon acquisition. That choice is what HAS caused the -28% drawdown since the Horizon announcement Oct 2023 (equity dilution via GCM and ECP + new debt). Disclosure is technically complete; framing minimizes how dependent the model is on continued capital-market access. Mode-B finding.

A coordinated multi-officer multi-director open-market purchase cluster within the explicit 10-Q open-window (Q1'24 10-Q was filed 2024-05-03) at prices ~25% below the deal-reference price is one of the strongest single forensic-disclosure signals available. Per the smallcap honesty framework, insiders putting personal capital in at the bottom of a -28% drawdown is the OPPOSITE of liar / obscuring behavior. Logged here at RED_FLAG severity to flag the polarity — the score recomputation should treat this as the strongest LONG-tier signal in the file. Honest-distress, not lying-distress.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify whether the 12-month liquidity claim is consistent with capex needs disclosed elsewhere. Mode B — derive: 10-K says capex will exceed continuing-ops cash flow through 2026 ($142.8M cash burn in 2023 alone); is the available liquidity enough to bridge to free-cash-flow positive?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Liquidity (lines 2597-2612) + 10-K Capex disclosure (line 2606: '$256.6 million exceeded our net cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations by $142.8 million') + Q1'24 pro-forma liquidity (line 3129: $484M total available liquidity including $109M cash, $225M delayed-draw term loans, $150M revolver)
rfm_tuples.M_value: At YE23: $239.3M available liquidity ($139.3M cash + $100M undrawn revolver). 2023 net cash burn (CFO - capex) was -$142.8M. So pre-Horizon, runway from cash alone was ~12 months at 2023 burn rate, extended by revolver to ~20 months. POST-Horizon-close (4/1/24): pro-forma available liquidity is $484M ($109M cash + $225M DDTL + $150M revolver), with debt-net-of-cash of $190M. Horizon adds revenue and EBITDA but also capex obligations. American Rescue Plan grants ($85.8M of which only a portion received) provide milestone-based cash inflow through 2026.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 12-month liquidity statement is well-supported by the pro-forma capital structure post-Horizon. With $484M available against ~$140M-$180M annualized capex-over-CFO gap, runway is ~2.5-3 years before another capital-markets transaction is required. This is exactly what the 'sufficient for next 12 months' boilerplate is designed to support — and it is genuinely supported. Not lying.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On October 1, 2023, the Company performed a qualitative analysis [of cable franchise rights impairment] and concluded there was no impairment.' (Critical Audit Matter / 10-K Note 6) — cable franchise rights $64.3M
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the no-impairment conclusion against the Q1'24 cable RGU trajectory disclosed in the 10-Q. Mode B — derive: if cable broadband-data RGUs inflected to YoY decline in Q1'24 (per C4 finding), does the qualitative impairment test from Oct 1, 2023 need to be revisited? rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 6 + CAM (lines 2630-2792) + Q1'24 KPI inflection per C4 + Q1'24 10-Q Note 5 (intangibles)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cable franchise rights carried at $64.3M (indefinite-lived). Qualitative assessment as of Oct 1, 2023 found no impairment. Q1'24 RGU data (per C4): Cable Markets data RGUs declined -0.9% YoY (vs +3.1% in 2022 and ~flat in 2023). Q1'24 10-Q does NOT disclose a triggering event for interim impairment testing despite the inflection. The CAM language ('high degree of auditor judgment ... use of our valuation specialist') means RSM was aware of the sensitivity. With Horizon closing 4/1/24 (which adds NEW franchise-type intangibles), management's qualitative test is rolling forward without quantitative validation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not a fraud finding, but the inflection in cable broadband data RGUs in Q1'24 — combined with the Oct 1 2023 annual test being purely qualitative — creates a setup where a future quantitative test could surface a partial write-down of the $64.3M asset. Disclosure is technically sufficient (the asset is broken out and the CAM exists), but the timing of the next quantitative test relative to the post-Horizon footprint reshuffle is a Mode-B watchpoint. Moderate.

summary: SHEN is a HONEST-DISTRESS profile, not a lying-distress profile. The -28% drawdown is driven by real economic stress — incumbent cable subscribers inflecting to YoY decline (Cable Mkts data RGUs -0.9% in Q1'24), heavy Glo Fiber overbuild capex exceeding CFO by $142M in 2023, a transformative $385M Horizon acquisition closed 4/1/24, and equity dilution via GCM (4.08M shares) and ECP ($81M preferred) — but every disclosure axis the framework probes is CLEAN: covenant compliance reaffirmed in Q1'24 with no relief amendments needed, Horizon timing delivered as guided ('first half of 2024' → April 1), T-Mobile customer-concentration churn quantified ahead of time and now materialized as disclosed, $484M post-close liquidity supports the 12-month statement, no going-concern language, no material weakness, ICFR unqualified, no Item 304 disagreements. The decisive signal is a coordinated multi-officer multi-director open-market purchase cluster (>=8 P-code Form 4s, May 7-13, 2024) by CEO/CFO/COO/CAO and directors at $14-17 — well below the $19.60 deal-reference price — within the Q1'24 open-window. Auditor downgrade KPMG->RSM in 2022 is a moderate yellow flag but pre-dates this filing by 18 months and shows no signs of dispute. Verdict: LONG-tier.
